Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
16 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.40 + 1.05 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 CNBC reports one Singapore-flagged ship was sunk in the strait, though maritime experts say Singapore vessels will keep transiting; this is not independently confirmed in this feed.

02 The New York Times reports oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz unexpectedly increased despite ongoing tanker attacks.

03 Brent stood at $105.40, up 1.05% over 24 hours, as of 06:15 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a live conflict zone, with attacks on commercial shipping continuing at an elevated pace. CNBC reports one Singapore-flagged vessel was sunk and that maritime experts say Singapore vessels intend to keep transiting the strait despite the strikes, reported on October 15; that account is not independently confirmed in this feed. Separately, News.com.au reports two vessels sank near the strait after being struck, and Asia Insurance Review reports two Singapore-registered vessels were struck, raising marine insurance risks. A tanker fire compounds the picture: econotimes.com reports the Iranian army says a tanker is burning near the strait, and Middle East Eye reports Iran's navy says a vessel described as a 'violating' oil tanker caught fire in the area. Al Jazeera reports containers are floating in the water after a vessel sank near the strait. Against that backdrop, the New York Times reports that oil flow through the strait unexpectedly increased despite the attacks. On the closure question, Press TV, econotimes.com, and WANA News Agency carry Major General Amir Hatami's statement, as an Iranian claim, that the strait is under complete supervision of Iran's armed forces and will stay closed until the enemy respects Iranian rights. Brent stood at $105.40, up 1.05% over 24 hours, as of 06:15 UTC. The feed indexed 79 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 06:22 UTC, 139 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
